rfm_tuples.R: Insider transactions implied claim: if management believes the Q1/Q2 FY25 results are sustainably improving and the cycle is stable, insider open-market selling should be modest and follow normal post-earnings trading windows; no clustering immediately before bad news.

All sales appear to be in post-earnings open windows; no sales immediately preceding the Sep 5 or Dec 5 earnings releases. Magnitudes are meaningful (CEO ~$7M in calendar 2024) but routine for a $4B+ market-cap company with long-vested grants. No sales after Dec 2024 — quiet during the Jan/Feb earnings blackout.

Sales are within open trading windows (not 10b5-1 plans disclosed in the captures) and appear technically routine, but the cluster magnitude and absence of insider buying is mildly bearish. This isn't a SEVERE signal — KFY's CEO has historically sold post-earnings — but the timing concentration warrants a small severity discount.

rfm_tuples.R: Q3 FY'25 Performance Highlights: Fee revenue in Q3 FY'25 was $668.7 million, flat year over year. RPO fee revenue increased 4% year over year and new business in Q3 FY'25 was $210 million, of which 64% and 36% was from new client wins and renewals/extensions, respectively.

Without Trilogy (Nov 1, 2024 close, $44.4M purchase), Professional Search & Interim would have declined modestly. Consulting -4.9% is real underlying weakness.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 'Flat' headline revenue is partially propped up by the Trilogy acquisition contributing one quarter of inorganic revenue. Organic growth is modestly negative across most segments. Management explicitly discloses the Trilogy effect on Professional Search & Interim (transparent) but does not provide an explicit organic-vs-acquisition reconciliation at the consolidated level. Not deceptive but selective framing.

rfm_tuples.R: On November 1, 2024, the Company completed its acquisition of Trilogy International ('Trilogy') for $44.4 million, net of cash acquired and recognized goodwill of $36.9 million.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: 83% of purchase price ($36.9M of $44.4M) booked as goodwill. Verify the acquisition is properly disclosed and that goodwill triggers no impairment indicator. Check whether KFY discloses Trilogy's standalone revenue/EBITDA.

Goodwill-heavy purchase is normal for a people business (no tangible assets). 25% of total assets in goodwill is elevated but supported by annual quantitative testing with stated 'no reporting units at risk'. Cannot verify Trilogy's standalone profitability from filings — small enough not to require segment-level disclosure.

Companies in genuine distress do not hike dividends 30% in March. This is the strongest single positive signal in the file.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'double-digit 20Y CAGR' is technically true (~11%) but the rate is heavily M&A-fueled and the current trajectory is contraction. Continuing to repeat the claim unchanged through 8 quarters of revenue softness is mild boilerplate puffery, not fraud. Forensic readers should discount this language.

summary: KFY is a clean, transparent staffing/talent firm disclosure with mostly PASS forensic signals. Balance sheet is fortress-grade (net cash $795M, undrawn $645M revolver, 4.625% Notes not maturing until 2027), auditor is Ernst & Young with 22+ year tenure and no Item 4.01 history, no material weakness, no going-concern language. FY24 restructuring ($68.6M, 8% workforce reduction) is functionally complete and EBITDA margin is expanding +190 bps YoY in Q3 FY25. Customer base is genuinely diversified (~15,000 clients, top 350 M&R accounts only 37% of revenue, no single client >10%). Counterparty mirror check is clean. The strongest positive signal is two pre-cutoff dividend hikes including a +30% bump declared March 10, 2025 — management-confidence behavior incompatible with internal expectations of deterioration. Three MODERATE flags: (1) CEO+CFO clustered $11M of open-market sales in a 2-week post-Q1 FY25 earnings window; (2) Q3 FY25 'flat' revenue is partially propped up by Trilogy inorganic contribution while underlying Consulting (-4.9%) and most segments are organically negative; (3) management continues to repeat the 'double-digit 20-year revenue CAGR' boilerplate despite two consecutive years of revenue contraction. None of these are red flags; the file looks like a cyclically-pressured but well-managed boring-middle name where the pre-cutoff drawdown reflects sector beta rather than idiosyncratic distress.
